newsitem.title: SPAIN: Amper will not confirm cashback report.
newsitem.headline: Amper will not confirm cashback report.

text.p: Spanish telephone equipment maker Amper SA said on Tuesday it would not confirm a report that it was studying a capital reduction through cash refunds to shareholders.
"I cannot confirm these types of speculations. Officially nothing has been communicated to me, but the board members have full freedom to propose what seems appropriate to them," a spokesman said.

A report in Spanish financial newspaper Expansion on Tuesday said Amper's board of directors was proposing to decrease capital by cutting the nominal share price and returning between 100 to 200 pesetas per share.

"The only official decision that the board has taken with respect to renumeration of the shareholders is to pay a final gross dividend of 45 pesetas. But this was already announced several weeks ago," the spokesman said.
Shares in the manufacturer rose 3.22 percent to 3,690 early on, settling to a 2.10 percent rise to 3,650 at midday with heavy volume of 365,000 shares traded.

Sector experts said that there has been frequent speculation about a possible cashback to shareholders since Amper reached a deal with German firm Siemens last year to sell Amper Elasa and Amper Datos to its Spanish unit for 14 billion pesetas.
